June 5, 1963 


FACULTY APPOINTMENTS & PROMOTIONS 


DOUGLASS" BURNS CLARKE, VICE*PRINCIPAL AT SIR GEORGE 
WILLIAMS UNIVERSITY ANNOUNCED 13 NEW APPOINTMENTS TO 

THE TEACHING FACULTY OF THE UNIVERSITY COMMENCING NEXT 
TERM AND © MAJOR FACULTY PROMOTIONS OF THE PRESENT STAFF. 


IN ANNOUNCING THE APPOINTMENTS, VICE~PRINCIPAL CLARKE 
STATED THAT THE UNIVERSITY 1S PROCEEDING ON A PLANNED 
PROGRAM OF ENLARGING STUDENT ENROLLMENT AND FACULTY DE}~ 
VELOPMENT TOGETHER OVER THE NEXT FOUR YEARS, THIS WAY, 
STUDENTS AND TEACHERS WILL NOT SUFFER FROM A MASSIVE AND 
SUDDEN EXPANSION WHEN THE NEW BUILDING 1S COMPLETED IN 
1966-67. WE ARE VERY FORTUNATE STATED PROFESSOR CLARKE 
TO BE ABLE TO ATTRACT SOME EXCELLENT TEACHING PEOPLE TO 
OUR FACULTIES OF ARTS, SCIENCE AND COMMERCE, 


AMONG THE FACULTY PROMOTIONS ARE TWO WELL-KNOWN FIGURES 

TO MONTREAL STUDENTS. H. HAROLD POTTER, ASSOCIATE PROFESSOR 
OF SOCIOLOGY, HAS BEEN NAMED PROFESSOR OF SOCIOLOGY, HAROLD 
POTTER 1S ONE OF SIR GEORGE'S EARLY GRADS, RECEIVING HIS B.A. 
IN 19,1 AND HIS M.A, AT McGILL IN 1947. ASSOCIATE PROFESSOR 
E.E. MCCULLOUGH, A GRADUATE OF QUEENS UNIVERSITY AND AN M.A. 
FROM McGILL, 1950, HAS BEEN NAMED PROFESSOR OF HISTORY.
